title: Eventual zero of affine higher-image sections
statement: Let Λ be an arbitrary commutative ring, k:W→S a scheme morphism and G a Λ-module sheaf on W_et [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Let I be a small cofiltered category, D:I→Over W an inverse system with affine transitions and qcqs composite structure maps to S, and c a cone whose underlying scheme cone is limiting, with qcqs composite structure map to S. Fix q∈ℤ and an affine etale object V→S. Write G_i=D(i)^*G and G_c=c.pt^*G [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]; write t for the canonical higher-image transition of [def-sbc-module-higher-image-transitions], using higher images as in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. For every i∈I and y∈(R^q(D(i)→S)_*G_i)(V) with t(c_i)(V)(y)=0, there exist j∈I and f:j→i such that t(D(f))(V)(y)=0. No assertion that limit sections admit representatives is made.

proof.text: Apply local eventual vanishing to obtain a covering sieve and an individual later-stage witness for every arrow in it.

The ranges of covering etale arrows are open and cover the affine object V. Compactness of V extracts a finite subfamily. Apply IsCofiltered.wideCospan to its witnessing arrows j_a→i, obtaining l→i and compatible arrows l→j_a. Transition coherence and naturality then show that the l-stage section restricts to zero on every member.

Apply sheaf separatedness on this finite covering. Form the module homomorphism Λ→R^q(D(l)→S)_*G_l(V) sending n to n times the transitioned section. All its restrictions are zero, so sheaf hom_ext_ofArrows makes this homomorphism zero; evaluation at 1 gives the desired zero section.

proof_origin.place: 09Z1 local continuity followed by the finite-cover injectivity argument of 0738(2); assembly proved using Mathlib compactness, wideCospan, and sheaf hom_ext_ofArrows

No Mathlib source hits for higher-image section continuity. Second reading with rg on both library roots and the source checkout also found AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.exists_higherDirectImage_affine_section_eq_zero in HigherDirectImageAffineSectionVanishing. It is an abelian-sheaf theorem for a directed preorder, nonnegative degree, and varying coefficients, not the general module-valued canonical-transition statement here. Its use would require reindexing and a natural module/abelian comparison. Abelian stalk analogues likewise do not directly match.
